item.content: {"url": "https://api.openalex.org/works?search=thermodynamic+entropy+production+bounds+predictive+information+coarse+graining&per-page=4&select=id%2Cdoi%2Ctitle%2Cpublication_year%2Ctype%2Ccited_by_count%2Copen_access%2Cprimary_location%2Cabstract_inverted_index", "scope": "OpenAlex scholarly metadata and reconstructed abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W4388092136\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2310.17929\", \"title\": \"Upper bounds on entropy production in diffusive dynamics\", \"publication_year\": 2023, \"type\": \"preprint\", \"cited_by_count\": 1, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"green\", \"oa_url\": \"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.17929\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"pmh:oai:arXiv.org:2310.17929\", \"doi\": null, \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"http://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17929\", \"pdf_url\": \"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.17929\", \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S4306400194\", \"display_name\": \"arXiv (Cornell University)\", \"issn_l\": \"2331-8422\", \"issn\": [\"2331-8422\"], \"is_oa\": true, \"is_in_doaj\": false, \"is_core\": false, \"listed_in\": [], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/I205783295\", \"host_organization_name\": \"Cornell University\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/I205783295\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [], \"type\": \"repository\"}, \"license\": null, \"license_id\": null, \"version\": \"submittedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": false, \"is_published\": false, \"raw_source_name\": null, \"raw_type\": \"text\"}, \"abstract\": \"Based on a variational expression for the steady-state entropy production rate in overdamped Langevin dynamics, we derive concrete upper bounds on the entropy production rate in various physical settings. For particles in a thermal environment and driven by non-conservative forces, we show that the entropy production rate can be upper bounded by considering only the statistics of the driven particles. We use this finding to argue that the presence of non-driven, passive degrees of freedom generally leads to decreased dissipation.
